title: Controlling Eutrophication along the Freshwater–Marine Continuum: Dual Nutrient (N and P) Reductions are Essential
organism: Phytoplankton / HABs along the freshwater-marine continuum
result: Argues that P-only controls upstream have worsened N-limited eutrophication downstream; both N and P reductions are needed along the continuum.
env_effects: Treats the cause; nothing added to the water.
key_details: Perspective essay by H.W. Paerl, not a new study. Main evidence is in situ nutrient-addition bioassays along the Neuse River Estuary, NC (N forms at 140 ug N/L, phosphate at 40 ug P/L, at 10, 25 and 50 km downstream) showing N limitation strengthening downstream of the chlorophyll maximum while P was sufficient. Argues against the Schindler et al. (2008) P-only view for estuarine and coastal systems and calls for dual N and P reductions. No treatment effect sizes.
fulltext_discrepancy: None; record should note it is an opinion/perspective piece supported mainly by bioassays from one estuary.

title: Determining Critical Nutrient Thresholds Needed to Control Harmful Cyanobacterial Blooms in Eutrophic Lake Taihu, China
authors: Xu Hui, Hans W. Paerl, Boqiang Qin, Guangwei Zhu, Nathan S. Hall, Yuchen Wu
scale: Six in-situ 1 L Cubitainer dilution bioassays (triplicate, 30-70% dilution, 2-day incubations; spring 2009-2012, August 2009, October 2010) plus an August 2013 N and P gradient bioassay in 100 L buckets (up to 10 days), Lake Taihu; mass-balance load model
dose: Dilution with N- and P-free major-ion solution, then N and/or P added back; August 2013: P 0-0.08 mg/L at fixed N 2.00 mg/L and N 0-1.00 mg/L at fixed P 0.20 mg/L, pulsed daily for 5 days
result: P limited phytoplankton in spring (DIN could be diluted 70% without reducing growth) and N limited it during the summer bloom. Recommended bloom-free targets (Chl a <20 µg/L) are 1.26 mg/L TN and 0.082 mg/L TP, which by mass balance require cutting external loads by 61-71% for TN and 20-46% for TP.
key_details: Nutrient-threshold study, not a test of an actual load reduction: short in-situ bioassays with natural phytoplankton, triplicate treatments, then a mass-balance model to convert in-lake targets into load targets (TN 15,707 and TP 1,640 x10^3 kg/yr vs current means of 46,000 and 2,170 x10^3 kg/yr). Microcystis made up 60-90% of bloom biomass. Internal sediment loading was estimated at 13-20% (TN) and 12-19% (TP) of external loads, and legacy sediment P is expected to delay recovery. Bottle/bucket incubations may not reflect continuous field nutrient supply, which the authors address with daily nutrient pulses.
fulltext_discrepancy: Record's thresholds (TN <0.80, TP <0.05 mg/L) are not the recommended management targets; the paper recommends 1.26 mg/L TN and 0.082 mg/L TP to keep Chl a below 20 µg/L. Setting is bioassays plus modelling, not mesocosm treatment of the lake.

title: Solving Problems Resulting from Solutions: Evolution of a Dual Nutrient Management Strategy for the Eutrophying Neuse River Estuary, North Carolina
authors: Hans W. Paerl, Lexia M. Valdes, Alan R. Joyner, Michael F. Piehler, Martin E. Lebo
dose: P-detergent ban (January 1988) and wastewater P-discharge limits in the late 1980s; later N reductions mandated by the Neuse River Basin TMDL
result: After the late-1980s P controls, upstream freshwater Chl a and nuisance cyanobacterial blooms dropped (very low mean annual Chl a in 1989) and upstream blooms stayed absent, with cyanobacteria giving way to chlorophytes and diatoms. But TN/TP rose most in the mid-estuary, where Chl a and blooms of dinoflagellates and cryptomonads grew larger in 1989-1992, 1994-1996 and 2000-2003, so the bloom zone moved downstream.
env_effects: Single-nutrient control moved the problem downstream; supports a dual N+P strategy.
key_details: Long-term monitoring analysis (1978-2003) of the Neuse River Estuary, not a controlled experiment. Upstream P-only control succeeded locally against cyanobacteria but the eutrophication gradient and Chl a maximum migrated downstream to N-limited mesohaline waters. Hurricanes and floods added large variability but, the authors argue, did not change the long-term pattern. Similar downstream shifts are cited for the Potomac/Chesapeake and Swedish Baltic fjords. Authors recommend dual N and P reductions starting upstream.
fulltext_discrepancy: Record frames the P-only outcome as 'likely shifted'; the paper documents a clear upstream success against cyanobacterial blooms plus larger mid-estuary blooms of dinoflagellates and cryptomonads (not cyanobacteria) afterwards.

title: Lake responses to reduced nutrient loading – an analysis of contemporary long‐term data from 35 case studies
authors: Erik Jeppesen, Martin Søndergaard, Jens Peder Jensen, Karl E. Havens, Orlane Anneville, Laurence Carvalho et al.
scale: 35 shallow and deep lakes in North America and Europe (latitude 28-65 deg), recovery periods 5-35 years
result: Summer chl a declined as TP fell in 71% of shallow and 69% of deep lakes; lake TP stayed above Vollenweider predictions for 5-10 years (internal loading) and reached a new equilibrium after 10-15 years. Cyanobacteria share declined in 80% of deep lakes, with no significant pattern in shallow lakes, where they stayed important down to ~50 ug TP/L.
env_effects: Internal loading delayed recovery; TN load cuts were smaller than TP cuts.
key_details: Synthesis of 35 case studies built on a questionnaire plus loading and lake data at maximum loading and every 5 years afterwards (3-year averages). All lakes had P-loading reductions, mostly beginning in the 1970s-1980s; three also had fish removal (Balaton, Veluwemeer, Apopka). Summer TP fell in 76% of shallow lakes and all deep lakes; phytoplankton biomass declined in 71% of shallow and 70% of deep lakes (not significant in sign tests). N response time was typically <5 years versus 10-15 years for P. There were no untreated control lakes, and some lakes (Peipsi, Vortsjarv) saw chl a rise despite load cuts, attributed to warming.

title: Eutrophication of lakes cannot be controlled by reducing nitrogen input: Results of a 37-year whole-ecosystem experiment
authors: David W. Schindler, Robert E. Hecky, D. L. Findlay, Michael P. Stainton, Brian R. Parker, Michael J. Paterson et al.
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
scale: Whole-lake experiment, Lake 227, Experimental Lakes Area
dose: Lake 227 fertilizer P held near 20-32 kg/yr throughout; N cut from 308 kg/yr (1970-74, N:P 12.4) to 110 kg/yr (1975-89, N:P ~4.7) to 0 (1990-2005)
result: After N fertilizer was cut and then stopped, N-fixing cyanobacteria (Aphanizomenon schindlerii) dominated and made up the N deficit; mean phytoplankton biomass (9,306 mg/m3) did not differ significantly among N:P periods, and annual chlorophyll a stayed 17-59 ug/L.
env_effects: Shows N reduction alone fails in this lake; P control needed (contested by dual-nutrient advocates).
key_details: Single whole-lake experiment (Lake 227, ELA, Ontario) fertilized 1969-2005 with nearly constant P while N input was reduced stepwise to zero; no replicate lake. N fixation (from heterocyst counts) was negligible before 1975 and rose after N:P was lowered. Biomass ranged 1,502-39,000 mg/m3 with no significant difference among periods; chlorophyll per unit biomass fell when N was scarce, so chlorophyll alone can mislead. Pike were added in 1993-1994 (food-web manipulation superimposed).
fulltext_discrepancy: None material; record lacked the load figures and the finding that biomass did not differ among N:P periods.

title: Toward Reversal of Eutrophic Conditions in a Subtropical Estuary: Water Quality and Seagrass Response to Nitrogen Loading Reductions in Tampa Bay, Florida, USA
authors: Holly S. Greening, Anthony J. Janicki
dose: Advanced wastewater treatment (TN <=3 mg/L, cutting that source's TN load by 90%), 1980s stormwater rules and port-facility BMPs; estimated total N load fell 60% (1985-2003 vs mid-1970s); later 'hold the line' at 1992-1994 load levels
result: Estimated N loading fell 60% from the mid-1970s to 1985-2003; Chl a declined significantly from 1985, most in Hillsborough Bay (25-35 µg/L in the mid-1970s to typically <15 µg/L), and Secchi depth there rose from <0.6 m to 1.0-1.4 m. Seagrass grew by 2127 ha from 1982 to 1996, lost 839 ha in 1996-1999 (El Niño) and regained 883 ha by 2004, the highest cover since 1950 but still 5512 ha below the 1950 extent.
env_effects: Reduced extent and duration of hypoxia; seagrass recovery. Projected 20% population growth and 7% higher N loading by 2010 require ~15.4 metric tons TN/yr of further reductions to hold the line.
key_details: Case study of Tampa Bay management using monthly sampling at >50 fixed sites since 1974 and biennial seagrass mapping since 1988. Point sources had made up 55% of N load before advanced wastewater treatment. Water-quality gains followed load cuts with no control estuary, so attribution is observational. Seagrass targets are set by the depth receiving 20.5% of surface light for Thalassia testudinum. Phytoplankton here is general Chl a, not a specific HAB taxon.
fulltext_discrepancy: Record lacks the 60% N-load reduction and the Chl a drop (25-35 to <15 µg/L in Hillsborough Bay); '25% seagrass increase since 1982' was not found as such, the text gives +2127 ha (1982-1996), -839 ha, +883 ha (to 2004), still 5512 ha below 1950.

title: Long-term nutrient reductions lead to the unprecedented recovery of a temperate coastal region
authors: Jonathan S. Lefcheck, Robert J. Orth, William C. Dennison, David J. Wilcox, Rebecca R. Murphy, Jennifer Keisman et al.
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
result: Water-column N fell on average 23% and P 8% since 1984; SAV cover rose 316%, from 7,878 ha (1984) to 24,874 ha (2015). Structural equation models link lower nutrients to SAV recovery, with P acting via phytoplankton chlorophyll-a and N acting directly (about 3x stronger than the chlorophyll/clarity path).
env_effects: Positive habitat recovery; nothing added to the water.
key_details: Observational analysis of 30 years of Chesapeake Bay aerial SAV surveys and water-quality monitoring using structural equation models (120 subestuaries coupled to watershed loads, plus a bay-wide model). No experimental control; attribution to management is by model. Outcome is seagrass cover, not phytoplankton or HAB abundance; chlorophyll-a appears only as an intermediate path from phosphorus.
fulltext_discrepancy: Record implies phytoplankton outcomes; the paper reports none directly (target is SAV). Adds that P fell only 8% and that the direct N effect outweighed the chlorophyll path.

title: Recovery of Danish Coastal Ecosystems After Reductions in Nutrient Loading: A Holistic Ecosystem Approach
authors: Bo Riemann, Jacob Carstensen, Karsten Dahl, Henrik Fossing, Jens Würgler Hansen, Hans Henrik Jakobsen et al.
dose: N loads cut ~50% and P 56% since 1990
result: Land-based N inputs fell ~50% and P 56% since 1990; annual mean chlorophyll a fell from a peak of 7 ug/L (1985) to ~2.5 ug/L, and Secchi depth rose only from ~4.2 m (early 1980s) to 5.1 m (2013). Bottom-water oxygen did not improve.
env_effects: Stratification and warming offset oxygen gains; filter-feeding benthos declined; Secchi gains modest.
key_details: Observational 25-year synthesis of Danish national monitoring data (nutrient loads, concentrations, chlorophyll a, Secchi, macroalgae, eelgrass, benthos, oxygen); no control area. Chlorophyll decline in spring followed P reductions; the continued decline since the mid-1990s mainly followed N reductions (May-October N limitation). Macroalgal cover rose 0.69%/yr and eelgrass spread deeper only in the last 5 years. Oxygen gains were offset by more frequent stratification and warming. effect_pct 64 is computed from the 7 to ~2.5 ug/L chlorophyll decline, not stated by the authors.
fulltext_discrepancy: Record had no phytoplankton magnitude; full text gives chlorophyll a 7 to ~2.5 ug/L. Secchi did not improve after 1990 despite the chlorophyll decline.

title: Inadequacy of best management practices for restoring eutrophic lakes in the United States: guidance for policy and practice
result: Restoring most eutrophic lakes needs >80% external P reduction, but watershed BMPs achieve at most ~50% and in practice <25%, explaining the few positive outcomes.
env_effects: Recommends supplementing with P inactivation or engineered treatment.

title: Phosphorus and nitrogen loading restraints are essential for successful eutrophication control of Lake Rotorua, New Zealand
authors: Val H. Smith, Susanna A. Wood, Chris G. McBride, Javier Atalah, David P. Hamilton
scale: Lake Rotorua, New Zealand; >10 yr data plus a global lake dataset
dose: Catchment N and P load targets (target TLI 4.2 needs TN and TP loads well below current); 496 t Al added as alum to 2 tributaries June 2006-June 2015
result: GAMs showed highly significant (p<0.001) declines in TP, TN and Chl-a in 2001-2015, and the target TLI of 4.2 was reached in 2012. Much of the improvement tracks tributary alum dosing: modelled TP fell from ~35 to 15 mg/m3 as dosing rose to 0.2 t Al/d, and Chl-a fell nearly 4-fold at the maximum 0.3 t Al/d.
env_effects: Includes alum dosing (aluminium addition) alongside catchment controls.
key_details: Case study of Lake Rotorua (New Zealand) using two >10-year water-quality datasets with generalised additive models, plus comparison with a global lake dataset, to argue for dual N and P control. Alum dosing entered the models as an 18-month rolling mean and had a highly significant negative effect on TP and Chl-a (p<0.001). Agriculture covers ~45% of the catchment and supplies an estimated 75% of the N load and 45% of the P load. The authors do not advocate alum dosing in perpetuity; success means removing alum while holding TLI <=4.2. Observational, with no control lake.
fulltext_discrepancy: Record credits catchment nutrient-load reduction; the paper attributes much of the 2001-2015 Chl-a decline to in-stream alum dosing (a chemical P-inactivation measure), with catchment load targets not yet met.

title: Eutrophication and harmful algal blooms: A scientific consensus
authors: J. Heisler, Patricia M. Glibert, JoAnn M. Burkholder, Donald Mark Anderson, William P. Cochlan, William C. Dennison et al.
result: Seven consensus statements, including that nutrient pollution promotes many HABs and that managing watershed nutrient inputs can lead to significant reductions in HABs.
key_details: Consensus paper from a 2003 US EPA-sponsored roundtable; review, no new data. Case examples: Seto Inland Sea red tides rose sevenfold (1965-1976), then fell to less than 30% of the peak frequency (>300 blooms/yr) after the 1973 law halving loads; phosphate removal from sewage on a Chesapeake Bay tributary reduced Microcystis blooms; Long Island brown tides nearly disappeared in the mid-2000s alongside N reductions. Correlational evidence only.
fulltext_discrepancy: None; record could add the Seto Inland Sea example (red tides fell to <30% of a >300/yr peak after loads were halved).

title: Contributions of external nutrient loading and internal cycling to cyanobacterial bloom dynamics in Lake Taihu, China: Implications for nutrient management
authors: Hai Yan Xu, Mark J. McCarthy, Hans W. Paerl, Justin D. Brookes, Guangwei Zhu, Nathan S. Hall et al.
dose: External loading 2005-2018: tributaries 16.6-24.1 g TN/m2/yr (mean 19.3) and 0.73-1.20 g TP/m2/yr (mean 0.89), plus atmospheric 3.8 g TN and 0.09 g TP/m2/yr; loads rose after 2007 to 2010, fell to 2013 and rose again to 2016, tracking inflow
result: Over 2005-2018, lake TN concentration fell 40% (p < 0.01) but TP did not decline, and annual mean Chl a rose slightly, peaking at 44 µg/L in 2017; annual TN and TP loading showed no relationship with Chl a. Internal P release supplied 23-90% of bloom P demand and water-column regeneration 38-58% of summer-fall demand.
env_effects: Denitrification removed 54% of external N; parallel N and P cuts recommended.
key_details: Whole-lake nutrient mass balance for Lake Taihu (2005-2018) from monitoring data, with estimates of burial, denitrification, water-column regeneration and internal P loading; observational, no control. Tributaries supplied 83% of TN and 91% of TP inputs, atmospheric deposition 16% and 9%, N2 fixation only 0.38% of TN. Authors expect a lag between load cuts and bloom decline because of legacy internal N and P, and argue that cutting N along with P gives faster recovery since denitrification removes N. Warming is expected to lower bloom nutrient thresholds.
fulltext_discrepancy: Record implies steady external load reductions; the paper shows external loads fluctuated with inflow (up 2007-2010, down to 2013, up to 2016) rather than declining steadily, TN concentration fell 40% while TP did not decline, and Chl a slightly increased.
